articles.title: Former US diplomat: Profit-driven foreign policy, American weapons enabled Gaza genocide
articles.body:
Former US diplomat: Profit-driven foreign policy, American weapons enabled Gaza genocide
TEHRAN — Hala Rharrit spent 18 years inside the United States State Department. She gave her adult life to American diplomacy. In April 2024, she walked away. She became the first American diplomat to resign publicly over the Biden administration’s actions in Gaza.
More than two years later, she views the institution she left behind as a hollowed-out machinery masking a profit-driven war apparatus.
In an interview with Middle East Eye published on August 31, Rharrit detailed a bureaucracy that systematically ignores war crimes, enriches military contractors, and treats Arab lives as expendable.
Her verdict leaves no room for ambiguity. American diplomacy in the Middle East is dead.
The receipts of complicity
Shortly after October 2023, Rharrit assumed a unique role as the Arabic-language spokesperson.
She says she refused orders to go on television and repeat State Department talking points that ignored Palestinian casualties and destroyed hospitals. Instead, she says she began compiling daily snapshots.
These intelligence briefs summarized Arabic-language media coverage and social media reactions, documenting the visual evidence of the carnage.
According to Rharrit, the reports traveled high up the chain of command. They reached an interagency task force, the assistant secretary for global public affairs, and the seventh floor where Secretary of State Antony Blinken sat.
Rharrit says she stuffed them with viral images of emaciated children and rubble. Career diplomats privately praised her.
Then the directive changed. In January 2024, the Bureau of Global Public Affairs told her the daily snapshots were no longer required. Washington had seen enough.
“At that point, it became evidence, right, of the war crimes,” Rharrit said. “It became evidence of everything that the administration actually did know. We’ve got the receipts. We know exactly what you knew when you knew it.”
A despicable public relations stunt
Recent media appearances by former Biden officials framing themselves as conflicted bystanders draw sharp contempt from Rharrit.
Former National Security Adviser Jake Sullivan and former spokesperson Matthew Miller have publicly expressed regret or conceded that Israel committed war crimes. Rharrit rejects this narrative outright.
“They’re so disgusting,” she said. “Those individuals, particularly Jake Sullivan and a handful of others, actually had the power to save human lives. They actually had the power to stop unconditional arms assistance to Israel.”
The scale of the destruction required Washington’s material support. “The Israelis were not killing the Palestinians by themselves,” she noted.
“The Israelis were killing the Palestinians with American bombs, with American jets, with American everything. We enabled it 100%. They enabled it 100%.”
She categorized their belated apologies as a cynical strategy born out of polling data.
Americans turned against forever wars. The former officials are simply trying to salvage their reputations to secure future employment.
The profit over people paradigm
Rharrit describes U.S. foreign policy through a strict financial lens. The military-industrial complex dictates outcomes. Democratic and Republican establishments both run on defense money.
The “Gaza pier” provides the clearest example of this structural greed. The project cost American taxpayers roughly $250 million. It functioned for barely 20 days.
It saved no one. The parallel airdrop campaign actually killed Palestinians when parachutes failed to open.
“Jake Sullivan did exactly what he was tasked to do,” Rharrit explained. “He made rich people richer. That was his mandate.”
This paradigm requires constant war. A destabilized West Asia allows Israel to pursue territorial expansion while U.S. military contractors secure endless government funding.
The Minab school massacre
This profit-driven model directly paved the way for the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. Rharrit sees the two wars as a single continuous front.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu sold Washington faulty intelligence, promising easy regime change and access to Iranian oil.
The tactical execution mirrored the worst of the Gaza campaign. Rharrit pointed directly to the American strike on an elementary school in Minab. The U.S. murdered at least 155 civilians in the attack, including over 120 children.
She dismisses the possibility of an intelligence failure or accidental targeting. The U.S. military possesses incredibly precise imaging capabilities. According to Rharrit, the strategy was intentional.
“We took straight out of the Israeli playbook of going straight after school, going straight after children,” she said. The strike was designed as a double-tap operation. “That means we hit. We waited for more people to come, and in this case, it was parents and teachers and other kids, and we hit again.”
The war failed its strategic objective. Rather than sparking a revolution against the Iranian government, the massacre unified the population against foreign aggression.
Now, Rharrit watches her former colleagues go on television to intellectualize the war on Iran. None of them mention the dead children in Minab.
‘They got over Iraq; they’ll get over this, too’
Before finalizing her exit from the government, she met with a highly influential State Department official.
Rharrit says she delivered a final warning. The unconditional support for Israeli atrocities was spawning a dangerous wave of anti-Americanism across the Arab world.
The official offered a chilling response. “They got over Iraq. They will get over this, too,” the official told her, referencing the Arab public.
Over one million Iraqis died due to U.S. sanctions and the subsequent military invasion. That conversation cemented Rharrit’s realization that human life held zero weight in Washington’s strategic calculations.
She harbors no regrets about walking away from her career.
“I am grateful every single day when I wake up that I resigned, that I’m free,” she said. “Nothing for me is worth me [sic] selling my soul.”

articles.title: US hits 3 Iranian tankers after IRGC fires missiles at Navy warships | Watch
articles.body:
U.S. forces struck three Iranian crude oil carriers on Saturday after Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps fired ballistic missiles toward two U.S. Navy warships patrolling regional waters, U.S. Central Command said, explaining explosions reported around Iran’s key oil-export hub of Kharg Island.
CENTCOM said a U.S. aircraft carrier and guided-missile destroyer successfully evaded multiple Iranian attacks and no American personnel were harmed. Following the failed strikes, U.S. forces permanently disabled the M/T Downy off Kharg Island and the M/T Stark 1 near Jask. A third vessel, the unladen M/T Kylo, also known as the Noxen, was completely destroyed in the Gulf of Oman after its crew was ordered to abandon ship.
American forces struck the Kylo in several critical locations to render it inoperable. CENTCOM said all three vessels were part of a multibillion-dollar shadow network used to fund the IRGC and its regional proxies. “Iran has no means by which to defend them,” the command said.
“Let the message to the IRGC be clear: If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost, taking out three of yours,” CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper said. “We will not hesitate to defend American forces, and if necessary, destroy Iran’s limited and exposed oil fleet.”
Video published by the opposition outlet Iran International and reportedly filmed from a nearby vessel captured what appeared to be U.S. warnings to the Stark 1 shortly before it was attacked.
“Stark 1 tanker, this is a U.S. aircraft. I am preparing to open fire on the stern of your vessel. You have three minutes to evacuate your personnel from the stern,” a voice is heard saying. A second warning reduced the deadline to one minute, followed by a final order: “This was your final warning. Get into your lifeboats and abandon ship immediately.”
Crew members can be heard speaking in Persian and Urdu. At one point, a crew member asks whether the captain and his deputy are at their stations and is told that the captain is still asleep. The Stark 1, which was carrying Iranian oil, was first placed under U.S. sanctions in 2018.
Iranian media earlier Saturday reported that a tanker had been struck roughly 10 kilometers from Kharg Island. The vessel was reportedly hit by four missiles while in the island’s anchorage area. No casualties were reported and its crew was evacuated. Iranian reports did not initially mention the two other vessels struck by U.S. forces.
The latest exchange follows a renewed escalation around the Strait of Hormuz this week. U.S. forces struck Iran’s Larak Island after Washington said Tehran was preparing to deploy naval mines in an attempt to disrupt a U.S.-led operation escorting tankers through the strategic waterway.
Iran responded with missile and drone attacks against neighboring Gulf states, prompting a broad U.S. wave of strikes against around 60 targets in the Hormuz region and southern Iran.
Tehran later launched further attacks across the region. Interceptions were visible Friday night over the Sea of Galilee, which the IDF said involved Jordanian activity. Iranian and other reports claimed missiles had been launched from Iran toward a U.S. base in Jordan.
President Donald Trump also renewed his threats against Tehran on Friday, saying the United States could soon strike Iran’s Fordow nuclear facility if developments there warranted it.
“We may hit Fordow very soon, because if something happens there, we’re not going to let it happen,” Trump said.
Trump rejected describing the confrontation with Iran as a war, instead calling it a “military conflict.”
“It’s not a big thing. It’s small money for us,” he said. “We lost 18 people, but in Vietnam you lost 100,000 people, and in other conflicts you lost tens of thousands. We’re carrying out strikes intermittently. It’s not a war.”

“Let the message to the IRGC be clear: If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost — taking out three of yours," said Admiral Brad Cooper, head of US CENTCOM.
Tasnim, the semi-official Iranian news agency, reported earlier that four US missiles hit a tanker in the area of Kharg's anchorage. Tasnim quoted local sources as saying there were no casualties and the tanker's crew was being evacuated.
No American personnel were harmed, CENTCOM said.
There was no immediate official announcement by Iranian authorities.
US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth took to X to write, "If Iran shoots at US ships, we will destroy (and sink) their oil tankers. All they have to do is not shoot at [the] US Navy."
The exchange of attacks follows an escalation in the past week that threatens to deepen a conflict that has dragged on since the US launched strikes on Iran in February, disrupting global energy supplies and drawing opposition from a majority of Americans before congressional elections in November.
Trump threatens Kharg Island
US President Donald Trump said on August 31 in a one-line social media post accompanied by an AI-generated video that Kharg Island was being "blown to smithereens". Iranian authorities have vowed a strong response if Kharg is attacked.
Iran is the third-largest producer in the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and exported 90% of its crude via Kharg Island before the war, but flows have been disrupted since a US blockade of Iranian oil exports began in mid-April.
Trump said on June 11 that he wanted to take over Kharg Island, but then said a threatened US military operation there was off the table for now, days before Tehran and Washington signed an interim agreement aimed at ending the war on June 17.
A US attack on Kharg would further pressure Iran's oil industry and its economy, which is already reeling from the US naval blockade.
The US imposed its blockade on Iranian ports after Iran effectively shut the Strait of Hormuz, an important waterway that carried one-fifth of the world's oil supply before the war.
Brent crude futures closed at their highest level since July 24 on Friday, at $96.28 a barrel, as tensions in the Middle East drive global supply concerns.

Russian Ballistic Strike Shuts Down Ukraine’s Kamet Steel Plant, Killing Five Workers
A Russian ballistic missile strike on the Kamet Steel plant in Kamianske, Ukraine’s Dnipropetrovsk region, killed five people, wounded four others, and forced the major steelmaking facility to suspend production.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
According to Metinvest, the plant’s parent company, on September 5, the attack occurred overnight and damaged Kamet Steel’s sinter and blast furnace operations, as well as energy and transport infrastructure across the industrial site.
Four Kamet Steel employees and one worker from a contractor were killed in the strike. Another four employees sustained injuries of varying severity and remain under medical supervision.
Only several minutes passed between the declaration of an air raid alert and the missile strike, Metinvest said, leaving some workers unable to reach shelters in time.
Oleksandr Myronenko, Metinvest’s chief operating officer, said there were no military facilities, equipment, or military production at the plant.
“Only civilians worked here, smelting iron and steel exclusively for civilian purposes,” Myronenko said.
Emergency and recovery operations are underway at the site. Specialists will be able to conduct a full assessment of the damaged equipment and infrastructure after debris removal is completed, according to the company.
Metinvest has not provided a timeline for restarting production. Kamet Steel is one of Ukraine’s major metallurgical facilities and produces pig iron, steel, and rolled products. The plant is part of Metinvest, one of the country’s largest industrial groups.
The September 5 attack marks the second time in recent weeks that a major Metinvest steel facility has halted operations following a Russian ballistic missile strike.
In August, Zaporizhstal suspended operations after a ballistic attack struck the facility shortly after an air raid alert was issued. Seven plant employees were killed and another 21 were injured in that attack.
Kamianske declared September 5 a day of mourning for those killed in the latest strike, while flags were lowered at Metinvest facilities.
The strike on Kamet Steel came during a broader Russian overnight attack on Ukraine on September 5. Russia also targeted Kyiv and Boryspil airports with Shahed-type drones, which President Volodymyr Zelenskyy linked to preparations for a possible US delegation arriving in Ukraine by air.

articles.title: US Envoys Witkoff and Kushner Arrive in Kyiv for First Visit
articles.body:
US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Kyiv on Sunday, Sept. 6, marking their first visit to Ukraine since the beginning of Russia’s full-scale invasion.
The US delegation arrived by train at Kyiv’s central railway station for direct negotiations with Ukraine’s leadership.

A senior Ukrainian delegation met the envoys upon arrival, including Head of the Office of the President Kyrylo Budanov, First Deputy Head of the Presidential Office Sergiy Kyslytsya, Head of the Foreign Intelligence Service (SZRU) Rustem Umerov, and “Servant of the People” parliamentary faction leader Davyd Arakhamia.
“Welcome to Kyiv, representatives of the President of the United States Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner,” Umerov wrote in a statement. “We continue close coordination on further steps to end the war.”
President Volodymyr Zelensky said that Ukraine had been preparing to welcome US President Donald Trump’s envoys at the airport.
“Unfortunately, the Russians made it clear with their attacks that they [Kushner and Witkoff] cannot use the plane, even though we had everything ready. Our airports are operational,” Zelensky said in comments to reporters, according to TSN.
He previously affirmed that Kyiv’s objective is to conduct a constructive and substantive dialogue with the US delegation, emphasizing that Ukraine remains focused on securing durable peace and robust security guarantees.
Ukrainian Dream: Thought Leaders on a Positive Vision for the Country
Subsequently, talks began in Kyiv with representatives of the US president, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, Zelensky stated on Telegram.
Strategy session and preceding Kremlin talks
The arrival of the US envoys follows a preparatory strategy meeting convened by Zelensky earlier Sunday with members of Ukraine’s negotiating delegation to finalize Kyiv’s diplomatic positions.
The Kyiv talks follow a three-hour-and-10-minute meeting between Russian President Vladimir Putin and the US delegation at the Kremlin on Saturday evening, Sept. 5.
Following those discussions, Russian presidential aide Yuri Ushakov claimed that Witkoff and Kushner agreed to factor Putin’s battlefield assessments into their dialogue in Kyiv.
Russian officials characterized the Moscow session – which also included an informal working dinner – as “meaningful,” “frank,” and conducted in an atmosphere of mutual trust, noting that potential large-scale US-Russian commercial projects were raised alongside conflict settlement concepts.
The broader Washington delegation visiting the region included officials from the National Security Council, the State Department, and the Treasury Department.
Gene Lange, acting head of the US Treasury’s sanctions division, traveled to Moscow and held a preparatory session with Kirill Dmitriev, Putin’s special representative for economic cooperation.
While Lange did not attend the direct session with Putin, his presence underscored that sanctions policy formed part of the dialogue, despite recent assertions by US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent ruling out economic concessions without an end to the war.
At the onset of the Moscow talks, Putin confirmed that Russian forces had paused aerial strikes on Kyiv starting at midnight on Sept. 5, but rejected Ukraine’s proposal for a wider three-day frontline ceasefire.
In reciprocal coordination to safeguard the diplomatic process, Zelensky previously pledged that Ukrainian forces would refrain from striking Moscow through Monday as the US envoys conduct their meetings.

Sources close to the Russian leadership indicated that Putin remains willing to end the war only on Russia’s terms, with the Kremlin hardening its demands amid a belief that it holds a decisive military advantage.
The sequence and timing of the diplomatic initiative also provoked scrutiny among Western officials and analysts.

Kremlin talks and Treasury involvement

Top US military officials face lie-detectors in hunt over classified stockpiles leak: Reports
- The Pentagon is conducting widespread polygraph tests on about 50 high-ranking military officials to find the source of leaked information on US munitions stockpiles.
- Reports of US rationing missile interceptors amid conflict with Iran were denied by officials, including President Trump, who confirmed some shortages of advanced weapons.
- The large-scale lie-detector use in this leak probe is unusual.
AI generated
WASHINGTON – The Pentagon has launched a lie-detector dragnet to comb through high-ranking military officials and identify who leaked information about US munitions stockpiles, according to US press reports.
In July, reports emerged that the United States was rationing munitions – its missile interceptors, in particular – over supply concerns after several months of fighting Iran.
Administration officials vehemently denied those reports, with President Donald Trump saying “we have a lot of ammunition, different types”, while acknowledging that “for some of the more sophisticated stuff, we’d certainly like to have more”.
Late on Sept 4, The New York Times reported that some 50 members of the military’s Joint Staff – the Pentagon’s planning and advisory staff – were being required to take polygraph tests as part of an investigation into how classified stockpile information made its way into journalists’ hands.
CBS News later also reported the wide-scale use of lie detectors, while adding that the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, General Dan Caine, had not been tested.
Both outlets cited unnamed officials.
Asked by AFP about the reports, the Pentagon’s chief spokesman, Sean Parnell, refused to comment on “internal personnel or investigative matters”, but said that it “takes all leaks of classified national security information extremely seriously and investigates accordingly”.
“Securing classified information is critical to ensuring the security of the United States and of our troops deployed around the world,” Parnell added.
Both the Times and CBS noted the scale of the polygraph testing.
Lie-detection testing is routine during background screenings and security clearance renewals for government staff with access to the most sensitive state secrets.
But the wide-scale deployment of the detectors as part of a leak investigation was rare, if not unprecedented, the outlets reported, citing analysts and unnamed officials. AFP

articles.title: U.S. forces destroy three Iranian oil tankers
articles.body:
- CENTCOM disabled or destroyed three Iranian oil tankers on September 5 after Iran fired ballistic missiles at two U.S. Navy ships, which evaded the attacks unharmed.
- The strikes follow a pattern since February's Operation Epic Fury, including a fragile June ceasefire and a July strike on more than 80 Iranian targets.
U.S. Central Command forces struck and disabled three Iranian oil tankers on September 5, hours after Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps fired ballistic missiles at two U.S. Navy warships patrolling the region, according to a CENTCOM statement.
Both American vessels, an aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer, evaded the Iranian missiles, and no U.S. personnel were harmed, CENTCOM said. The command did not name the two ships involved.
In response, American forces permanently disabled two Iranian crude oil carriers, the M/T Downy off Kharg Island and the M/T Stark 1 near Jask, and completely destroyed a third, the unladen M/T Kylo, also known as the Noxen, in the Gulf of Oman. CENTCOM said forces struck the Kylo in multiple critical locations after its crew was ordered to abandon ship, rendering the vessel inoperable.
CENTCOM described the three tankers as part of what it called a multibillion-dollar shadow fleet that generates revenue for the IRGC and its regional proxy groups, adding that Iran had no way to defend the ships once they were targeted.
“Let the message to the IRGC be clear: If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost, taking out three of yours,” said Adm. Brad Cooper, CENTCOM commander. “We will not hesitate to defend American forces, and if necessary, destroy Iran’s limited and exposed oil fleet.”
The strikes are the latest exchange in a conflict between the United States and Iran that began February 28, when the U.S. launched Operation Epic Fury. American forces have since enforced a naval blockade meant to cut off Iran’s oil exports, repeatedly disabling tankers that attempted to defy it. In May, an F/A-18 launched from the USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN 72) disabled the tanker M/T Hasna’s rudder with cannon fire near an Iranian port, and jets from the USS George H.W. Bush (CVN 77) later disabled two more unladen tankers, the M/T Sea Star III and M/T Sevda, attempting the same route.
A ceasefire took hold by early June, though CENTCOM described it as fragile at the time and publicly disputed Iranian claims that its forces had fired on U.S. Navy ships in the Gulf of Oman, saying doing so would have violated the truce. The uneasy calm broke down further in July, when Iran struck three commercial tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, prompting CENTCOM to hit more than 80 targets across southern Iran overnight, including air defense systems, command-and-control networks, coastal radar sites and more than 60 IRGC small boats.

articles.title: China’s latest Middle East play makes Egypt a pivot of power
articles.body:
China’s latest Middle East play makes Egypt a pivot of power
Xi Jinping’s state visit to Egypt, which began on September 1, was his first in a decade and coincided with the 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries.
During his meeting with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, Xi called on Middle Eastern states to become masters of their own destiny, resist outside interference, and discuss a new regional security architecture. Beijing and Cairo agreed to deepen cooperation on security and counterterrorism, develop projects with data centers, semiconductors, and critical minerals, and expand the use of national currencies in bilateral trade. The relationship is moving beyond conventional trade and infrastructure into sectors that will shape economic sovereignty for decades.
The agenda fell within China’s familiar formula – development, state sovereignty, and fairer global governance. Beijing increasingly presents itself as a voice for the global majority and the Global South, where many countries associate today’s instability with Western hegemony, US sanctions, and decades of attempts to reorder other regions by force. Wars, regime change campaigns, economic blockades, and the division of states into “acceptable” and “unacceptable” have brought the Middle East neither lasting peace nor promised prosperity. Instead, they have created zones of chronic conflict, and made dependence on foreign patrons a source of regional vulnerability.
Beijing offers a different model of engagement, built around infrastructure, trade, investment, and recognition of every state’s right to choose its partners and development path. China is not doing this out of charity – its policies serve the world’s largest industrial economy, which needs export markets, secure transport corridors, and reliable access to raw materials. Even so, many countries in the Global South find it more attractive than a Western approach often accompanied by political conditions, sanctions threats, and demands to accept an external hierarchy of priorities. Chinese investment can also create debt as well as technological, and trade dependencies, but it rarely entails overt supervision of a partner’s domestic order. That distinction allows Beijing to work with very different governments that share a desire for greater freedom of action.
Xi’s visit to Cairo is thus a part of a broader Chinese initiative to strengthen ties with countries seeking a multipolar order and to set constructive interdependence against the destructive effort to preserve a unipolar system. Egypt occupies a special place in this strategy – it is simultaneously an Arab, African, and Mediterranean power, capable of anchoring China’s presence across several regions at once.
Egypt: China’s gateway to Africa
For China, Egypt offers a rare combination of strategic advantages. With a population of more than 110 million, it has a large domestic market, controls the Suez Canal, carries considerable political weight in the Arab world, and provides direct access to African markets. One of the principal maritime routes between Asia and Europe passes through Suez, making Egypt’s stability directly relevant to the security of Chinese foreign trade. Cairo is becoming a bridge between the Middle East, the Mediterranean, and Africa, where China has steadily expanded its economic and political influence.
China–Africa trade reached a record $348 billion in 2025, while Beijing’s removal of tariffs on imports from 53 African countries strengthened its position just as the US was returning to protectionism. Africa’s importance to China goes well beyond mineral resources. Its rapidly growing population needs roads, power plants, ports, telecommunications, and industry – all areas in which China has extensive capacity. By building infrastructure and manufacturing hubs, Beijing opens markets for Chinese companies, embeds long-term commercial ties, and converts economic presence into political capital.
Egypt is particularly important because of the Suez Canal Economic Zone, which, according to the Egyptian government, has already attracted around $4 billion in Chinese investment. Chinese companies are involved in port and railway development, construction of the New Administrative Capital, pipe and tire manufacturing, green energy projects, and satellite production. Total accumulated Chinese investment in Egypt exceeds $10 billion, while bilateral trade reached a record $20.79 billion in 2025. In the first half of 2026 alone, trade rose by a further 21.5% to $11.3 billion. Egyptian exports to China roughly tripled over the same period, although their absolute value, at $840.8 million, remained far below the volume of Chinese goods flowing in the opposite direction.
This imbalance remains the main economic contradiction in the partnership. Egyptian imports from China reached roughly $10.4 billion in the first half of the year, and Cairo cannot remain merely a market for Chinese products. It must move from importing finished goods to localizing production, securing technology transfers, creating jobs, and integrating Egyptian companies into transregional value chains. If Chinese industrial zones support component manufacturing, workforce training, and exports to Africa, the Arab world, and Europe, the partnership will become more balanced. Otherwise, impressive figures will continue to conceal dependence on foreign supplies and a persistent trade deficit.
China’s presence also broadens Egypt’s room for manouver in foreign policy. Cairo receives approximately $1.3 billion in US military assistance each year and remains close to Washington while developing ties with China, Russia, and BRICS. El-Sisi calls this a strategic balance, reflecting the Global South’s wider desire to diversify partnerships and escape junior status within a Western-led system. Beijing supports that choice, because every industrial project, logistics terminal, or yuan-denominated transaction turns multipolarity from a slogan into material reality.
The limits of neutrality
The Middle East’s importance to China is most clearly expressed in numbers. Trade between China and the Arab states reached $407.4 billion in 2024, with Chinese exports accounting for $206 billion and imports for $201.4 billion. Behind this apparent balance lies a critical energy dependence. In 2025, the Middle East supplied around 52% of China’s oil imports, or approximately 1.9 billion of the 3.6 billion barrels it purchased abroad. Six Arab suppliers in the Gulf provided 42% of all Chinese oil imports: Saudi Arabia accounted for 14%, Iraq 11%, the United Arab Emirates 7%, and Oman 6%. The region also supplied nearly one-third of China’s liquefied natural gas imports, most of it from Qatar.
For China, stability in the Middle East is an economic necessity. Rising oil prices increase industrial and transport costs, while any threat to the Strait of Hormuz affects several major suppliers at once. The Red Sea and Suez Canal are equally important: disruption forces ships around Africa, lengthening delivery times and raising insurance costs, especially for China-Europe trade. Beijing is diversifying suppliers, developing pipelines, building strategic reserves, and accelerating its shift to renewable energy, but it cannot quickly replace Middle Eastern supplies without substantial costs.
Iran occupies a distinct place in this equation. According to estimates by the global trade analysis company Kpler, China imported around 1.38 million barrels of Iranian oil per day in 2025, equivalent to roughly 12% of its total oil imports. Sold at a discount of about $8-10 a barrel, Iranian crude remains an attractive resource for Chinese industry, while Beijing’s purchases provide vital support to an Iranian economy under sanctions. Yet Saudi Arabia and the UAE are far more important to China in terms of overall trade. In 2025, Chinese trade with each country reached approximately $108 billion, compared with an estimated $41 billion with Iran once unrecorded oil shipments are included.
Beijing maintains a strategic partnership with Tehran, exceptionally close relations with Pakistan, expanding ties with the Gulf monarchies, and support for Palestinian statehood, while avoiding commitments that could draw it into a regional war. Chinese diplomacy aligns with Iran in opposing external military pressure and unilateral sanctions, and with the Arab majority in supporting an independent Palestinian state. At the same time, economic interdependence compels Beijing to maintain working relations with every major regional actor, including Israel.
Beijing has neither sent troops to defend Tehran against the US and Israel nor turned the relationship into a military alliance. It prefers diplomacy and trade, and refuses to recognize unilateral restrictions. China seeks not one regional power’s triumph, but an equilibrium that safeguards commerce, keeps maritime routes open, and prevents an outside hegemon from determining the region’s future.
Regional security without a new hegemon
The final element of China’s proposition concerns global and regional governance. Xi has urged Middle Eastern states to determine their region’s future and limit external interference – an appeal that has found a receptive climate.
The Gulf states, Egypt, and Türkiye continue to cooperate with the US while expanding ties with China, Russia, India, and one another, because recent experience has exposed the risks of excessive reliance on US security guarantees. Washington still commands the region’s largest network of bases and alliances, yet this power has failed to produce durable order and has often accompanied new wars and divisions.
The Mecca joint defense agreement signed by Saudi Arabia, Türkiye, and Pakistan on August 7 expressed this desire for greater autonomy. It establishes that an armed attack on one member will be regarded as an attack on all, although practical mechanisms remain undefined. Egypt’s possible accession would give the grouping far greater political and military weight. Beijing views its underlying logic favorably as regional responsibility, diversified partnerships, and reduced external dependence accord with China’s understanding of multipolarity, while Pakistan links the emerging framework to one of Beijing’s closest partners.
It would nevertheless be wrong to cast China as a selfless champion of the Global South or a future replica of the US. Beijing pursues its own interests and uses its economic scale to promote Chinese companies, standards, and currency. Its instruments, however, are different. Beijing does not organize regional policy around regime change, divide partners by ideology, or build military protectorates. Nor is it prepared to replace the US as an all-encompassing security guarantor or immerse itself in the region’s religious, national, and dynastic rivalries.
China’s influence is growing by other means: trade, investment, technology, ports, energy contracts, diplomatic mediation, and support for the autonomy of regional powers. This strategy has already produced tangible results. Saudi Arabia and Iran restored relations through Chinese mediation in 2023; BRICS expanded; China-Arab institutions grew stronger; and the gradual shift towards settlement in national currencies began. None of these developments alone will displace the dollar or erase Western military and political influence. Together, however, they are weakening one center’s monopoly on writing the rules.
Xi Jinping’s visit to Egypt marks the next stage of that process. China remains cautious about the use of military power, but its expanding economic presence is increasingly translating into political influence. Its ability to engage simultaneously with Iran, the Arab monarchies, Egypt, Türkiye, Pakistan, Palestine, and Israel makes Beijing a natural participant in any future regional security system. For the global majority, what matters is the principle embodied in this presence: a major power that does not demand unconditional loyalty, but helps broaden the choices available to the states of the Global South and reinforces their sovereignty.
That is why China’s approach is increasingly regarded across the region as a substantial counterweight to US-led Western hegemony. This is not simply about replacing one global leader with another, but about creating an order in which no power can impose its will on everyone else. Egypt, linking Asia, Africa, and the Mediterranean, can become one of its pillars. Xi’s visit shows that multipolarity is ceasing to be a diplomatic abstraction and is acquiring infrastructure, trade routes, financial mechanisms, and political agency.

articles.title: France can’t finance Ukraine forever – Le Pen party head
articles.body:
France can’t finance Ukraine forever – Le Pen party head
France lacks money for itself and simply cannot keep funding Ukraine indefinitely, Jordan Bardella, the president of Marine Le Pen’s right-wing National Rally (NR) party, has said.
The main French opposition party faced harsh criticism from its rivals earlier this week after its vice president, Louis Aliot, said that NR “would turn off the tap” for Kiev if it comes to power after the 2027 presidential vote. Le Pen is seen as having strong chances to succeed in the election next year, no matter who her rival will be in the second round.
Bardella weighed in on the issue during his speech at the Ambrosetti Forum in Italy on Saturday, saying that Ukraine needs support from France and other Western nations during the conflict with Russia, but “our objective should not be to finance the war ad vitam æternam,” which means ‘forever’ in Latin.
France has a national debt of €3.5 trillion ($4.6 billion) and cannot be “giving money that we no longer have” to Vladimir Zelensky’s government, he argued.
“The extremely serious and worrying state of French public finances means we can’t give money without any guarantees or assurances that this money will be repaid one day,” the National Rally president said.
Paris has been one of the strongest backers of Kiev in the EU after the escalation of the Ukraine conflict in February 2022, providing it with billions in military aid and supplying various sophisticated weapons, including CAESAR self-propelled howitzers and Mirage fighter jets.
According to Bardella, the Americans were “much smarter” than the Europeans when it came to assistance for Kiev “because the money they gave to Ukraine is secured against rare earth mining.” He was referring to the deal agreed upon between Washington and Kiev last year, which grants the US preferential access to Ukrainian mineral resources.
During US President Donald Trump’s second term, Washington also significantly reduced aid to Ukraine, making European NATO members pay for American-made arms supplied to the country.
Earlier this week, Trump warned that he intends to present Europe with a belated bill for billions of dollars that Washington spent arming Ukraine under his predecessor, Joe Biden. He previously estimated that Biden gave Zelensky more than $300 billion worth of weapons for “free.”
Le Pen said on Thursday that the National Rally is skeptical about further assistance to Ukraine because it believes that the conflict with Russia needs a diplomatic solution.
A poll by Harris Interactive in late August suggested that Le Pen has the support of 34% of the French public, which should guarantee her a place in the second round of the presidential election, where she would likely win comfortably against either her left-wing rival Jean-Luc Mélenchon or the centrist candidate, former Prime Minister Edouard Philippe.
Russian officials said repeatedly that foreign weapons being sent to Kiev will not prevent Moscow from achieving its military goals, but will merely prolong the fighting, while increasing the risk of a direct confrontation between Russia and NATO.

articles.title: Ukraine’s drone forces say they hit 58,465 Russian targets in August, nearly 1,900 a day. Three named campaigns did the strategic damage
articles.body:
Ukraine's drone forces say they struck 58,465 Russian targets in August, an average of nearly 1,900 a day. The tally is up almost 9 percent on July and more than double January's, and it included 54 vessels of Russia's shadow fleet, 33 air-defense systems, and 168 energy nodes, Unmanned Systems Forces commander Robert "Madiar" Brovdi reported on his Telegram channel.
The volume matters less than where some of it lands. Cutting power to occupied Crimea and the south is meant to blind Russian air defense, much of which runs on the grid. Meanwhile, the strikes on Russia's sanctions-evading shadow fleet squeeze both Crimea's fuel supply and Moscow's oil exports.
Ukraine's drone forces claim 11,010 Russian troop casualties in August
Brovdi also said the strikes killed or wounded 11,010 Russian soldiers over the month, about 355 a day — a figure that counts only losses the drone force attributes to its own strikes, not Russia's total casualties.
That daily rate was slightly below July's 374, down about 5 percent, even as the number of targets rose. Compared with January, the force said Russian personnel losses were up 17.3 percent.
Three campaigns inside the count
Most of the headline volume is small front-line targets, but three named operations account for the strategic hits. Under Operation "Milk", the force said it struck 54 shadow-fleet vessels in August, bringing the total to 260 since the campaign began on 6 July. Operation "PPOpad" — a play on the Ukrainian for air defense — hit 33 Russian air-defense elements in August and 263 across 2026.
The third, Operation "Crimean Switch Off", struck 168 energy nodes in August, bringing the total to 349 since early July. That campaign has been running for months, blacking out swaths of occupied Crimea.
Brovdi has argued that cutting power to stationary radars and other air-defense elements opens the airspace for deeper Ukrainian strikes. Months of these strikes have left occupied Crimea rationing fuel and living with rolling blackouts, and cut the Kerch ferry crossing's capacity by about three-quarters. All of the figures are the force's own, and Ukraine's military claims of Russian losses are not independently verified.

articles.title: Kremlin and White House call Trump envoys' Moscow talks "constructive and substantive"
articles.body:
Kremlin and White House call Trump envoys' Moscow talks "constructive and substantive"
After talks between Russian ruler Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump's representatives Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner ended, the Kremlin highlighted the key points of the discussions. The White House described the talks as "substantive".
Source: Kremlin-aligned Russian news agency TASS, citing Putin's aide Yuri Ushakov; Reuters, citing a White House representative
Details: Ushakov described the meeting as "substantive, constructive and exceptionally frank".
He said Putin's talks with the US negotiators lasted three hours and 10 minutes.
Putin's aide added that Witkoff and Kushner "promised to take into account in tomorrow's meetings in Kyiv Putin's assessments of ways to reach a settlement".
Quote from Ushakov: "The US representatives were thoroughly prepared for their trip to Moscow and formulated a number of considerations on ways to reach a settlement.
Putin and Trump will maintain personal contact, while the work mediated by Witkoff and Kushner will also continue."
Details: In addition, Ushakov said the talks were not limited to Russia's war against Ukraine, with possible major Russian-US projects also discussed.
At 01:20 Kyiv time, Russian media reported that Witkoff and Kushner's plane had left Russian airspace.
It was later reported that the negotiators' plane had landed in Rzeszów, Poland.
Update: A White House representative told Reuters that the talks had been "substantive" and that the next steps would be announced in the coming weeks.
Background:
- On 5 September, Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow. They went to the Kremlin after a business lunch with Kirill Dmitriev, Putin's special envoy. The US negotiators are expected in Kyiv on 6 September.
- On the afternoon of 5 September, the Kremlin announced that Putin has ordered that no strikes be carried out on Kyiv for three days, starting from midnight.
- After speaking with Trump's special envoys, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Kyiv is willing to halt airstrikes on the cities involved in the negotiating process.

articles.title: Ukraine Defence Contact Group to meet next week, says Kyiv
articles.body:
Ukraine Defence Contact Group to meet next week, says Kyiv
Ukraine's Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara and his German counterpart Boris Pistorius have held a phone call, during which they discussed preparations for a meeting of the Ukraine Defence Contact Group (also known as the Ramstein format) to be held next week.
Source: Ukraine's Ministry of Defence, as reported by European Pravda
Details: Khmara briefed Pistorius on Russia's ever-intensifying air terror, emphasising that the key threats are jet-powered drones and ballistic missiles.
Khmara said Ukraine is developing its own defence plan and taking asymmetric action that is yielding results. Meanwhile, strengthening protection against Russian strikes as quickly as possible remains a priority.
The two sides discussed funding for defence needs. Ukraine's Defence Ministry is conducting an audit of resources and human capital within Ukraine's defence forces. However, financial support from Kyiv's partners remains critically important to Ukraine's resilience.
The ministers also focused on preparations for the Ramstein-format meeting next week and discussed closer cooperation between the Ukrainian and German defence industries.
Khmara thanked Germany for its significant support and leadership in working with other partners of Ukraine.
Background:
- The last meeting of the Ukraine Defence Contact Group was held on 18 June at NATO Headquarters in Brussels and was co-chaired by the United Kingdom and Germany.
- Following the meeting, Pistorius announced that Ukraine would receive a three-digit number of air-to-air missiles from German stocks. He also said the two nations would jointly produce ground robotic systems.
- On the same day, Ukraine and Germany signed a defence agreement concerning the joint development of an air defence system capable of intercepting ballistic missiles.

articles.title: Ukraine ready to halt strikes on cities involved in US-mediated peace talks: Zelenskyy
articles.body:
Burc Eruygur
05 September 2026•Update: 05 September 2026
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Saturday that his country is ready to halt strikes on cities involved in US-mediated efforts to negotiate a settlement to the Russia-Ukraine war.
In a statement on US social media company X, Zelenskyy said he spoke with US envoys who traveled to Moscow for talks earlier in the day and that they had already begun their work in Russia.
“From the moment of this conversation, we are ready to observe a ceasefire in airstrikes against the cities involved in the negotiation process.
“From now through the end of Saturday, as well as on Sunday and Monday, Ukraine is ready to refrain from strikes on Moscow, and we expect the Russians to do the same regarding Kyiv,” Zelenskyy added.
The Ukrainian president’s statement came after the Kremlin said Russian President Vladimir Putin had ordered a three-day halt to strikes on Kyiv beginning at midnight local time (2100GMT).
Earlier Saturday, US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow for talks aimed at finding a settlement to the more than four-year conflict.
The US envoys are expected to visit the Ukrainian capital Kyiv on Sunday for the first time following their Moscow trip.
Trump said Friday that Kushner and Witkoff would travel to Moscow not with new ideas, but with a proposal aimed at ending the war.
“They’re bringing with them a proposal to end the war,” Trump said, referring to the two negotiators.

articles.title: Zelensky Meets Negotiators Ahead of Talks With US Envoys
articles.body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky convened a strategy session with members of Ukraine’s negotiating delegation on Sunday, Sept. 6, ahead of scheduled talks with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.
In a statement on Facebook, Zelensky confirmed that the Ukrainian team had finalized its negotiating positions, emphasizing that Kyiv remains committed to a constructive approach aimed at bringing a definitive and just conclusion to the war.

“A meeting with our negotiating team. Ready for the conversation,” Zelensky stated. “Ukraine has always been and will always be constructive. We are interested in bringing an end to the war closer. Peace is needed. Security guarantees are needed. A dignified character of post-war peace is needed.”
The president stressed the necessity of disciplined, coordinated, and realistic diplomatic engagement, underscoring that Ukraine’s core objectives center on durable security arrangements and sovereignty.
Envoys arrive in Kyiv following Kremlin talks
The Kyiv consultations follow a three-hour-and-10-minute meeting between Russian President Vladimir Putin and the US delegation at the Kremlin on Saturday evening, Sept. 5.
Following those discussions, Russian presidential aide Yuri Ushakov claimed that Witkoff and Kushner agreed to factor Russian President Vladimir Putin’s frontline assessments into their dialogue in Kyiv.
Russian officials characterized the Moscow session – which also included an informal working dinner – as “meaningful,” “frank,” and conducted in an atmosphere of mutual trust, noting that potential large-scale US-Russian commercial projects were raised alongside conflict settlement concepts.

The broader US delegation visiting the region included officials from the National Security Council, the State Department, and the Treasury Department.
Gene Lange, acting head of the US Treasury’s sanctions division, traveled to Moscow and held a preparatory session with Kirill Dmitriev, Putin’s special representative for economic cooperation.
While Lange did not attend the direct session with Putin, his presence underscored that sanctions policy was part of the dialogue, despite recent assertions by US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent ruling out economic concessions without an end to the war.
At the onset of the Moscow talks, Putin confirmed that Russian forces had paused aerial strikes on Kyiv starting at midnight on Sept. 5, but rejected Ukraine’s proposal for a wider three-day frontline ceasefire.
In reciprocal coordination to safeguard the diplomatic process, Zelensky previously pledged that Ukrainian forces would refrain from striking Moscow through Monday as the US envoys conduct their meetings.

articles.title: US envoys meet with Putin, leave Russia for Kyiv
articles.body:
US envoys meet with Putin, leave Russia for Kyiv
Published September 5, 2026last updated September 6, 2026
US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Saturday evening.
"The situation is of course not simple," Putin told the US officials in footage aired on Russian state media.
Putin and US envoys held "useful" talks on a range of ideas to end the war in Ukraine, Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov told reporters.
According to Russian media outlets, US envoys left Moscow after the meeting.
Earlier, US President Donald Trump said Kushner and Witkoff were traveling to Russia with a new proposal, but he did not provide any details on the potential peace plan, including whether it involved Ukraine giving territory to Russia as he has previously suggested. Instead, he said, "We have an idea for peace."
In the meeting with Putin, Kushner and Witkoff discussed "substantive plans" for the next steps toward ending the Ukraine war, the White House said, adding that more details would be announced next week.
The envoys "look forward to equally productive meetings tomorrow in Ukraine," a White House official said in a statement.
Russia, Ukraine pause strikes for three days
The Kremlin said Russian forces would pause strikes against Kyiv for three days in conjunction with the peace negotiations.
Putin "ordered that no strikes be carried out against Kyiv for three days, starting at midnight today," Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov told state media.
The order came after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had already committed to pausing airstrikes for the talks.
"As with previous diplomatic visits by the American side, we will ensure the normal functioning of Russian airspace so that the negotiators can arrive safely. We are concerned about their safety, not about Russia," Zelenskyy said.
US envoys to make first visit to Kyiv
Zelenskyy announced on Friday that Kushner and Witkoff would visit Ukraine on Sunday following talks in Moscow.
Recent media reports have questioned whether the pair would indeed travel to Ukraine. Despite trips to Moscow to meet with Russian officials, the US envoys have not visited Kyiv since Trump's reelection last year.
On Saturday, Zelenskyy said he had been in contact with Kushner and Witkoff.
"I have just spoken with the US president’s envoys," Zelenskyy said on Telegram.
"From the moment of this conversation, we are ready to observe a ceasefire in airstrikes against the cities involved in the negotiation process."
Trump had promised to end the war in Ukraine, now in its fifth year, on his first day back in office, but has more recently said that the feat was more complicated than expected. In the past, he has blamed Ukraine for the Russian invasion and a "personality problem" between the countries' leaders for the continued fighting.

articles.title: Russia attacks military plants and logistics across Ukraine – MOD (VIDEO)
articles.body:
Russia attacks military plants and logistics across Ukraine – MOD (VIDEO)
The Russian military has conducted large-scale drone and missile strikes on Ukraine, targeting assorted dual-use infrastructure sites, industry, and shipping in the Black Sea, the Defense Ministry in Moscow said on Saturday.
The ministry named a broad range of targets hit over the past 24-hour period, including two major metal plants in Dnepropetrovsk Region, which have been supplying cast iron and steel to the Ukrainian defense industry.
Footage circulating online suggests the plants sustained considerable damage, with major fires erupting onsite.
The Russian military hit multiple logistic centers and stockpiles across the country, including warehouses in the Odessa, Nikolayev, and Kiev regions. The strikes also targeted two fuel depots near the Gostomel airfield outside Kiev, as well as an electronic reconnaissance point in Brovary on the outskirts of the Ukrainian capital, the ministry said.
Footage shared by the ministry features drone strikes on Ukrainian shipping. Two dry cargo vessels and a container ship were hit at the port of Chernomorsk. Another dry cargo ship was struck at the port of Odessa, the ministry said.
All the vessels were hit by jet-powered Geran-4 Seeker drones, the ministry noted. The Seeker family of drones are said to be fitted with AI-powered machine vision systems, which enable the UAVs to search for, identify, and lock onto targets without input from their operators.
Over the past month, Moscow has drastically ramped up long-range strikes against Ukraine, with the campaign coming in retaliation for Kiev’s efforts to damage Russia’s energy sector and shipping. The retaliatory campaign has effectively brought Ukrainian shipping in the Black Sea to a halt, as well as heavily disrupted ground logistics within the country.
The latest wave of strikes comes ahead of a three-day hiatus in attacks on Kiev ordered by Russian President Vladimir Putin ahead of talks with senior US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who arrived in Moscow on Saturday. The pause in the strikes on the Ukrainian capital is intended to allow US President Donald Trump’s envoys to attend negotiations with Ukrainian officials in the country’s capital, according to Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov.

Fresh Yemen clashes kill more than 60
Fighting between Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces and the country's Houthi rebels killed more than 60 people on Saturday, including civilians, medical and military sources told AFP.
The renewed clashes in Yemen's southwest over control of a gateway to the Red Sea came after Friday saw some of the deadliest fighting in years, following the collapse in July of a 2022 ceasefire.
According to three Yemeni military sources, 26 government troops were killed during several hours of fighting in the country's southwest, while medical and military sources from the Iran-backed Houthis said 31 rebel fighters were killed.
One medical source in the government-held city of Taiz said a missile strike also killed six civilians travelling by bus and wounded seven others.
A government official blamed the strike on the bus, travelling between Taiz and the seat of Yemen's internationally recognised government in Aden, on the Houthis.
In Taiz, a military officer said the "coming hours will be decisive" after the Houthis seized positions near the city a day earlier.
The officer added that reinforcements had been arriving from Aden in response to the Houthi offensive, which aims to cut off the government-held port city of Mokha, under fire for weeks, and advance towards areas bordering the Bab al-Mandab strait.
On Friday, the fighting killed 129 people, according to an AFP tally compiled from several sources.
With Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz to commercial ships, the Bab al-Mandab chokepoint has gained importance as a transit route for oil from Saudi Arabia, the world's biggest exporter of crude.
A military official told AFP on Saturday that three airstrikes by Saudi Arabia, a key backer of the government in Aden, had targeted positions recently captured by the Houthis in Taiz.
In July, a fragile truce between the Houthis and Yemen's government fell apart after the rebels welcomed an Iranian plane to the capital Sanaa, setting off a spate of attacks.
The fighting between the Iran-backed Houthis and government troops supported by US ally Saudi Arabia signals the emergence of a new front in the wider Middle East war, which broke out in late February with US-Israeli strikes on Iran.
The Houthis have also announced a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and have begun targeting its ships and territory.

Ukraine Blinds Russian Defenses in Bryansk, Hitting Radar, EW System and MESH Network
Ukrainian forces struck several Russian military systems in Russia’s Bryansk region, including a radar station, an electronic warfare complex, and a relay supporting a MESH communications network.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
According to Ukraine’s General Staff on September 5, the strikes were carried out on September 4 and targeted military infrastructure at three separate locations across the region.
A Russian radar station was hit near Kartushino, while an electronic warfare system was targeted in the area of Pogar. Ukrainian forces also struck a MESH network relay in Zlynka, the General Staff said.
The General Staff did not identify the specific models of the radar or electronic warfare systems involved, meaning their exact capabilities and value cannot yet be independently assessed.
Radar stations are used for tasks ranging from airspace surveillance and target detection to supporting air defense and other military operations. Electronic warfare systems can be employed to detect, disrupt, or suppress radio communications, navigation signals, and drone control links.
The MESH relay represents a different part of the communications infrastructure. In a mesh network, individual nodes can relay data between one another rather than relying exclusively on a single central communications point.
Such architecture can extend communications coverage and provide alternative routes for data if individual links are disrupted. The General Staff did not specify which Russian MESH system was targeted or what units it supported.
Ukrainian forces also struck a repair facility used by a Russian military unit in Sokolohirsk in the temporarily occupied Luhansk region.
“The extent of the damage is being clarified. Work on the enemy’s key military targets continues. More to come!” Ukraine’s General Staff said.

articles.title: US military says it destroyed 3 Iranian oil tankers after missile attacks
articles.body:
Berk Kutay Gokmen
05 September 2026•Update: 05 September 2026
US Central Command (CENTCOM) said Saturday that its forces struck and disabled three Iranian crude oil tankers after the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) launched ballistic missiles toward two US Navy warships in regional waters.
 
In a statement shared on US social media company X, CENTCOM said an aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer successfully evaded multiple Iranian attacks, adding that no American personnel were injured.
 
According to the statement, US forces permanently disabled the M/T Downy off the coast of Kharg Island and the M/T Stark 1 near Jask. They also destroyed the unladen M/T Kylo, also known as the “Noxen,” in the Gulf of Oman after its crew was ordered to abandon ship.
 
CENTCOM said the vessels were part of a “multibillion-dollar shadow network” allegedly used to finance the IRGC and its regional proxies.
 
“Let the message to the IRGC be clear: If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost -- taking out three of yours,” CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper said.
 
“We will not hesitate to defend American forces, and if necessary, destroy Iran’s limited and exposed oil fleet,” he added.
 
Iran’s state broadcaster IRIB confirmed that the US military had attacked three Iranian oil tankers: one near Kharg Island in the Gulf and two off Jask in the Sea of Oman.
 
No casualties were reported in the Kharg Island attack, while a fire was extinguished aboard the tanker. Of the two tankers off Jask, one was empty and the other was carrying oil, while their crews were evacuated ashore in lifeboats, IRIB said.
 
Regional tensions have escalated since US-Israeli attacks on Iran began on Feb. 28, with Tehran responding with missile and drone strikes against Israel and US interests across the region.
 
Washington and Tehran signed a memorandum of understanding in June concerning freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, but its implementation has stalled amid disagreements over security arrangements in the strait.

articles.title: Germany prepares comprehensive "protective shield" against Russian sabotage
articles.body:
Germany prepares comprehensive "protective shield" against Russian sabotage
Following a failed attempt to attack Leipzig/Halle airport with an explosive-laden drone, Germany plans to strengthen protection against Russian sabotage and other hybrid attacks.
Source: German tabloid Bild, as reported by European Pravda
Details: German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt is planning a package of measures covering protection against drones and sabotage targeting critical infrastructure and cyberattacks, as well as the detection of spies and potential terrorists.
"Russia's hybrid attacks using explosive-laden drones targeting airports, agents in our cities, cyberattacks on our networks and sabotage of our infrastructure are a daily reality. These attacks will intensify, but we can fight back and protect ourselves," Dobrindt said.
According to Bild, Germany plans to expand the Federal Police's mobile anti-drone unit.
The new units, which can be rapidly deployed to different areas, will have helicopters and special vehicles. They will be stationed in nine strategically important cities: Frankfurt am Main, Munich, Hamburg, Berlin, Stuttgart, Düsseldorf, Leipzig, Hanover and Cologne.
Their task will be to protect the airspace above key transport hubs, airports, railway stations and the government district in Berlin. This will involve not only detecting and intercepting drones, but also disabling explosive-laden UAVs.
Another proposal involves expanding the powers of companies operating critical infrastructure. Water utilities, energy companies and defence industry facilities could be given legal powers not only to detect drones but also to actively counter them. This should allow them to respond more quickly to attacks on critical infrastructure facilities without waiting for state forces to arrive.
The plan also envisages wider use of AI, biometric facial recognition and video surveillance systems, particularly at railway stations. AI would help automatically detect weapons and suspicious behaviour, as well as identify people suspected of preparing attacks or engaging in espionage.
Another area is protection against cyberattacks. The plan calls for the creation of a national Cyberdome – an extensive network of digital sensors designed to detect and block attempted hacker attacks.
Background: On 1 September, Germany directly accused Russia of a hybrid attack at Leipzig airport in early August and announced countermeasures.

articles.title: Putin pauses strikes on Kiev
articles.body:
Putin pauses strikes on Kiev
Russian President Vladimir Putin has ordered a three-day hiatus in strikes on Kiev ahead of talks with senior US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who arrived in Moscow earlier on Saturday.
The negotiations are expected to focus on resolving the Ukraine conflict. Witkoff and Kushner are slated to visit Kiev after their meetings in Moscow, which include talks with Putin.
Speaking on Saturday, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said that “Russian president [and] commander-in-chief Putin has ordered [the armed forces] not to conduct strikes on Kiev for three days starting from midnight today.” He added that the decision was intended to allow Witkoff and Kushner to hold negotiations with Ukrainian officials in the country’s capital.
Several Ukrainian media outlets carried reports earlier in the day, saying that Kiev’s forces had been instructed to hold their fire starting from Saturday midnight until Tuesday.
Ukrainian broadcaster Suspilne subsequently quoted Vladimir Zelensky’s chief of staff Kirill Budanov as saying that Ukraine had sent a truce proposal to Russia calling for the temporary cessation of hostilities along the front line, as well as all air strikes. However, Moscow did not respond, according to Budanov.
On Friday, US President Donald Trump said that Witkoff and Kushner were “bringing with them a proposal to end the war,” without elaborating on the specifics.
Since the start of Trump’s second term in office in early 2025, the two negotiators have repeatedly visited Moscow as part of the US president’s efforts to mediate a peace deal between Russia and Ukraine.
However, despite a glimmer of hope following last year’s meeting between Trump and Putin in Alaska, the diplomatic back-and-forth has since stalled as neither Russia nor Ukraine will compromise on key issues.
Still, speaking on Thursday, the Russian president praised Kushner’s and Witkoff’s work, saying that the US negotiators are “always welcome guests here, and we work with them with pleasure.”

An Iranian crude oil tanker has sunk in the Gulf of Oman after being struck by American forces, US Central Command (CENTCOM) has said. It was one of three commercial vessels targeted by the US on Saturday after Iran launched ballistic missiles at two American warships.
The M/T Kylo went down in the Gulf of Oman, CENTCOM said in a post on X on Sunday. The oil carrier “joined Iran’s navy at the bottom of the sea,” it added.
CENTCOM published drone footage showing the half-submerged vessel, with plumes of smoke coming from it. The US military said the M/T Kylo had not been carrying oil and that its crew had been directed to abandon ship before it was struck.
The attack follows renewed US-Iran hostilities earlier this week. Washington launched strikes on Iran on Tuesday, prompting Tehran to retaliate against US facilities in the Gulf with missiles and drones.
The US military described Iran’s missile launches against its aircraft carrier and guided-missile destroyer as unsuccessful and “unprovoked.” It claimed the three vessels it subsequently targeted were part of “a multibillion-dollar shadow network” financing Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).
“Let the message to the IRGC be clear: If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost – taking out three of yours,” CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper said in a statement.
Tehran has confirmed that three Iranian tankers were attacked and damaged by US forces, but has not confirmed that the M/T Kylo sank. The Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters warned that Washington would face even “more severe” strikes against its military vessels across the region should it continue to “harass” Iranian shipping and maintain a blockade on the country’s ports.
In response, the IRGC said it had struck three oil tankers that were “trespassing” in the Strait of Hormuz, along with three US-linked vessels, in retaliation for the American attacks.
The IRGC later said it had fired several ballistic missiles at a US aircraft carrier and a destroyer. “After sustaining damage and fearing another reprisal, the two warships were forced to flee the area of engagement,” it claimed. CENTCOM, however, said the vessels had successfully evaded the Iranian attacks and that no American personnel were harmed.
Tehran had previously warned that it would retaliate against oil and gas infrastructure belonging to US allies in the Gulf if its own oil infrastructure, particularly facilities on Kharg Island, were attacked or Washington attempted to seize the island.

Russian attacks killed at least nine people and injured at least 68 across Ukraine over the past day, Ukrainian authorities reported on Sept. 6.
Firefighters were deployed in both Kyiv Oblast and Dnipropetrovsk Oblast to extinguish large fires following Russian attacks.
Two people in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast were injured, said the Governor Oleksandr Hanzha. No casualties were reported in Kyiv Oblast at the time of publication.

Among those killed were an 11-year-old boy and a 19-year-old woman in the town of Chuhuiv.
In Kherson Oblast, three people were killed, and a further 19 were injured, including two children, said Governor Oleksandr Prokudin.
Russia killed one person and injured a further 25 in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, said the local military administration. Attacks later in the morning injured two women.
In Mykolaiv Oblast, Russian Shahed drone attacks on transport infrastructure killed one driver in the Halytsynove community, said Governor Heorhii Reshetilov.
Russia injured two people in Donetsk Oblast and forced a further 915 people, including 136 children, to be evacuated from front-line areas, said the region's governor, Vadym Filashkin.
Seven people, among whom was one child, were injured by falling debris from a Russian drone in Khmenytskyi Oblast, said Governor Serhii Tyurin.
